title: docs(agents): drop the retired "gen:schema wipes gen:openapi" trap from three agent-facing surfaces
body:
Fixes #11597

Three agent-facing surfaces still taught the pre-#5371 trap "`gen:schema`'s cleanup wipes `gen:openapi`'s output" and prescribed a `gen:openapi` rerun to recover from it. The trap is gone; the docs are not. This deletes the stale clauses.

## Current behavior, from the source

`build-schemas.ts` no longer removes the output directory itself. Its clean routes through `clearOwnedOutputs()`, which skips every entry declared in `FOREIGN_JSON_SCHEMA_ARTIFACTS` — and `openapi.json` is the one entry there.

- `packages/spec/scripts/lib/json-schema-out-dir.ts:70-72` — `FOREIGN_JSON_SCHEMA_ARTIFACTS` maps `openapi.json` to `'gen:openapi (packages/spec/scripts/build-openapi.ts)'`.
- `packages/spec/scripts/lib/json-schema-out-dir.ts:121-125` — the clean loop: an entry present in that map goes to `preserved` and is skipped, never removed.
- `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts:297-323` — the clean calls `clearOwnedOutputs(OUT_DIR, …)` instead of the old `fs.rmSync(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true })`, and line 318 prints `↳ kept openapi.json — owned by gen:openapi (…) (#5371)` for each spared entry.
- The fix commit is `83f86077cd` — *"fix(spec): gen:schema clears only its own outputs, sparing gen:openapi's openapi.json"*. (The card cites this as #5371; the commit subject carries `(#6200)`. Both refer to the same landed change; `83f86077cd` is an ancestor of this branch's base `dd4113ec`.)

Pinned in two layers, both already in the tree:

- `packages/spec/scripts/json-schema-out-dir.test.ts:78` — *"leaves gen:openapi's openapi.json byte-identical"* (unit).
- `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts:2113` — *"build-schemas.ts — the output clean spares a sibling generator (#5371)"* (integration), carrying a `--check`-specific case because `check:authorable-surface` was the reported trigger.

No destructive generation command was run to establish this — the evidence above is read from the current source, per the dispatch constraint.

## The file list is the grep's, not the card's

The card names two files. A repo-wide grep for the claim (`wipes` / `抹掉` / `清场` / `expected 503 to be 200`, intersected with `openapi` / `gen:schema`) returns **three** surfaces, four occurrences:

| Surface | Occurrence |
| --- | --- |
| `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` | :190-192 — the dispatch prompt itself |
| `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md` | :20-21 |
| `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` | :28-30 header comment **and** :105-106 |

The third is not named in the card, and its second occurrence is the worst of the four: it is inside the step-4 heredoc the script **prints to the operator at run time**, so an agent reads the retired trap as live instruction on every merge of a generated-artifact branch.

Two remaining hits in `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` are deliberately left alone: they state a different and still-true fact (`gen:docs` dropping a reference page when a schema stops being emitted), and a changelog is a historical record rather than an agent-facing instruction.

## Deleted rather than restated

The guarantee and its full reasoning already live at the source, in the `json-schema-out-dir.ts` docblock, pinned by the two tests above. Restating it in three agent prompts would spend budget on a non-trap; the prompts' job is to warn about live ones. `AGENTS.md` was already corrected and is untouched here.

The MERGE-state anchor trap sitting beside each deleted clause is **unaffected and still true** — it is kept verbatim in all three files. One knock-on: `landing-operations.md` introduced the pair as `顺序防两个陷阱` ("the order prevents two traps"), which becomes `顺序防的陷阱`. Only one of the two was ever an ordering trap; leaving the count would have been a second false statement.

Line deltas (all reductions, nothing rewritten):

| File | Before | After | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` | 405 | 403 | −2 |
| `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md` | 82 | 80 | −2 |
| `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` | 112 | 108 | −4 |

`.claude/skills/` package total: 2595 → 2593 (−2). This is internal agent tooling under `.claude/`, not the customer-published `skills/` directory, so the published-skills budget ruling does not apply; the numbers are reported anyway because the surface is skill-adjacent.

## Governed surface — draft, human merge

Two of the three files are under `.claude/**` (one of them the dispatch prompt itself), so Prime Directive #14 applies: **this PR stays draft, is never queued, never auto-merged, and is not flipped out of draft by an agent.** The PM decides the landing path.

## Verification

Gate families derived mechanically with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no path arguments — the script reads its own change set). 14 families matched; all run green, plus the 3 artifact-roster families the residue flags as *"not evidence in EITHER direction"* for paths under `scripts/` and `scripts/pm/`, which were run rather than reasoned about.

**Union re-run at final commit `5c49c442`**, exit codes captured before any pipe. Each gate's own verdict line:

`check:doc-formula-expressions` first came back exit=1 on a missing `@objectstack/formula/dist` and then on `packages/lint/dist` — the unbuilt-closure trap in a fresh worktree, not a finding. It is green above only after `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build` **and** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint build`.

`bash -n scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` exits 0 (the edit touches a heredoc, so the parse is load-bearing). A control-byte self-scan over the three edited files (`grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]'`) returns no match.

**Changeset: none, deliberately.** Nothing published moves — `.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**` are repo-level agent tooling, in no package's published `files`. `skip-changeset` applied.
